segments.text: I'm collecting 14 million data points on exactly what happens in my menstrual cycle. This will be a world first for female health, but every second of my day will be monitored by a 12-person medical team. Here is my unhinged schedule.

>> [music] >> First thing I do when I wake up is spit into a tube to collect my cortisol reading. So we'll be able to compare that day to day. We'll also be tracking how my metabolism changes. Does it increase? Do I burn fats and carbs differently? We'll also be doing things like smell sensitivity and taste sensitivity. The irony is that I'm a creative, chaotic human being. I do not do well with schedules. So why am I doing this unhinged routine? Because female health is not understood. And a big part of my motivation is that if we can put words to the female experience, others will be able to understand it.

And if we can understand it, we can respect it. It's also just helpful to articulate for ourselves what's going on in our own bodies. So this is just to collect baseline measurements. I'll be doing this for around 100 days. From there, I'll be doing interventions to see what happens when I do X intervention, how does that affect my biology? We'll be posting everything here for free, so follow along if you're interested in learning more.
